//: TRUST POLICY for the GitHub Actions deploy role (rules.md R-55).
⚠️ DO NOT PASS THIS FILE TO THE AWS CLI. It is annotated source; the `"//"` key is not legal in an
IAM policy document and AWS rejects the whole thing with `MalformedPolicyDocument: Syntax errors in
policy`, naming no key and no line. Render it first — which also substitutes the placeholders:
python scripts/render_iam_policies.py --account-id <ID> --github-owner <O> --github-repo <R>
then use infra/iam/rendered/gh-actions-trust-policy.json. The renderer refuses on any leftover
placeholder, which matters most HERE: an unsubstituted <AWS_ACCOUNT_ID> in a trust policy is not a
loud failure. The ARN simply matches nothing, `create-role` succeeds, and every deploy fails later
with an OIDC error that points at GitHub rather than at this file.
OIDC only. There are no long-lived AWS access keys anywhere in this project — not in repository
secrets, not on a laptop. GitHub presents a short-lived signed token, AWS verifies it against the
OIDC provider, and STS issues credentials that expire with the job. A leaked workflow log cannot
leak a credential that no longer exists.
PREREQUISITE: the OIDC identity provider must exist in the account first. It is created once, by
hand, in Phase 0 (aws-setup-instructions.md §4). Its ARN is the Federated principal below.
REPLACE BEFORE USE: <AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>, <GITHUB_OWNER>, <GITHUB_REPO> — via the renderer above, not
by editing this file. Editing it in place is how the placeholders end up committed with a real
account id in the diff.
THE TWO CONDITIONS ARE BOTH LOAD-BEARING, and omitting either is a known account-takeover shape:
1. `aud` = sts.amazonaws.com. Without it, a token minted for a different audience is accepted.
2. `sub` restricted to THIS repo. Without a `sub` condition, ANY GitHub repository in the world
— anyone's — can assume this role. This is the single most common OIDC misconfiguration.
The `sub` patterns are deliberately narrow: main-branch pushes and the protected environment only.
Feature branches and pull requests cannot assume this role, which is what makes `git push` unable
to touch AWS at all (rules.md R-29) rather than merely unable to start GPU spend.
NOTE ON `ref:refs/heads/main`: it is written with StringLike but contains no wildcard, so it is an
exact match. It is in the StringLike block only to sit alongside the environment pattern, which
also has none — both are exact by design. A `repo:OWNER/REPO:*` pattern would readmit every branch
and every pull request, which is precisely what this is preventing.
